title: Kernel-to-range inclusion for the constructed Tor boundary
statement: For every commutative ring R, modules M,F,N and surjective q:F → N, every Tor class killed by the constructed boundary lies in the image of Tor₁(q,M).

proof.text: Import all Sheaf.Paper.TorLongExactFirstVariable and apply its existing private resolutionSES to the kernel inclusion and q. This yields projective resolutions A, B, C with compatible augmentations and degreewise splittings. Tensor the splittings with M to obtain a short exact sequence S of complexes.

Identify H0(A tensor M) with ker(q) tensor M using the existing private homologyZeroIso imported from Sheaf.Paper.TorLongExactFirstVariable. Identify H1(B tensor M) and H1(C tensor M) with Tor via isoLeftDerivedObj; its naturality identifies the homology map of b with Tor₁(q,M).

Apply the signed horseshoe comparison theorem to identify the transported homology connecting map with the negative of torKernelBoundary. If torKernelBoundary(y)=0, injectivity of the degree-zero isomorphism shows that the connecting map kills the image of y in H1(C tensor M). Apply S.homology_exact₃ to obtain a preimage in H1(B tensor M), then transport it through the Tor isomorphisms and use naturality to obtain the required range witness.

proof_origin.note: Complete Lean proof of the horseshoe plan with a proved signed connecting-map comparison. The existing resolutionSES and homologyZeroIso helpers are used through a proof-only import all Sheaf.Paper.TorLongExactFirstVariable; no local copies remain.

theorem tor_kernel_boundary_construction_exact_left_kernel
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (M : ModuleCat.{u} R)
    (F N : ModuleCat.{u} R) (q : F →ₗ[R] N) (hq : Function.Surjective q) :
    ∀ y, torKernelBoundary M F N q hq y = 0 →
      y ∈ Set.range (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) 1).map
        (ModuleCat.ofHom q)).app M).hom
